body:
With NX8's 8-bit static formats, the tensor that loses most even in its best format is layernorm output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256: 32.1 dB SQNR (signal-to-quantization-noise ratio; higher is better) in fp8_e2m5, measured on that tensor alone by the format search. Measured on 41 models with a format search (of 289 surveyed).

Model outputs keep a median 23.1 dB SQNR against full precision, the worst 2.8 dB (Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct). 23 of 31 models with a prediction metric (top-1, perplexity or agreement) lose some of it; the most: microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (agreement 100% → 0%: the share of samples whose predicted class matches full precision's), PaddlePaddle/PP-DocLayoutV3_safetensors (agreement 100% → 0%: the share of samples whose predicted class matches full precision's) and Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (perplexity 16.5 → 94.5, higher is worse).

The tensors that lose most in their best format (their own error): layernorm output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 32.1 dB), linear bias in Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (fp8_e3m4, 33.0 dB), layernorm bias in Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B (fp8_e2m5, 33.3 dB), linear bias in mattmdjaga/segformer_b2_clothes (fp8_e2m5, 33.5 dB), linear bias in SamLowe/roberta-base-go_emotions (fp8_e2m5, 33.6 dB), linear bias in deepset/roberta-base-squad2 (fp8_e2m5, 33.6 dB), linear output in Arunavaonly/Bangla-twoclass-Sentiment-Analyzer (fp8_e3m4, 33.8 dB), linear bias in facebook/bart-large-cnn (fp8_e2m5, 33.9 dB), add output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 34.0 dB) and embedding output in BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 (fp8_e2m5, 34.1 dB).

Separately, the error accumulated along the data path (every tensor before a node quantized too): reciprocal outputs end furthest from full precision, PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 keeping only -inf dB there. The outputs furthest from full precision in each model's best format set: reciprocal in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, -inf dB), mul in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, -inf dB), div in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, -inf dB), log in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, -inf dB), reciprocal in PaddlePaddle/PP-DocLayoutV3_safetensors (fp8_e3m4, -inf dB), mul in PaddlePaddle/PP-DocLayoutV3_safetensors (fp8_e3m4, -inf dB), div in PaddlePaddle/PP-DocLayoutV3_safetensors (fp8_e3m4, -inf dB), log in PaddlePaddle/PP-DocLayoutV3_safetensors (fp8_e3m4, -inf dB), div in microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (fp8_e3m4, -inf dB) and amin in PaddlePaddle/PP-DocLayoutV3_safetensors (fp8_e3m4, -758.2 dB, with full precision's selection forced).

Formats chosen (E = exponent bits, M = mantissa bits, u = unsigned): fp8_e2m5 19595 (59%), fp8_e3m4 9431 (28%), fp8_e1m6 4080 (12%), fp8_e4m3 2 (under 0.01%); 0% of tensors use an unsigned format.

A wider format or a per-row choice would recover most where a tensor's own error in its format, times its data, is largest: softmax output in openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo (fp8_e2m5, 37.4 dB), softmax output in openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo (fp8_e2m5, 37.7 dB) and softmax output in openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo (fp8_e2m5, 38.7 dB).

title: NX8 formats: layernorm output keeps only 32.1 dB in its best format

body:
8 missing capabilities keep 162 operations in 26 models (of 39 planned) off the chip's direct path; the most widespread is run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip) (77 operations in 24 models). In two sections, each ranked by the MACs its gaps hold:

### Substitute proposed or evaluated (5 gaps)

**Run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip).** The chip cannot read memory at an address computed at run time, so every lookup or choice by a run-time value (embedding, gather and select_where) needs a workaround. It affects 77 operations in 24 models: 77 calls (0.48% of all calls) and no MACs (data movement only); the biggest: embedding in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256, gather in PaddlePaddle/PP-DocLayoutV3_safetensors and embedding in SamLowe/roberta-base-go_emotions. Cost today: 0 of 77 have a workaround (0 exact, 0 approximate), 0 failed and 77 wait for one; 191 workarounds proposed, 121 passing its check, 83 evaluated on a model; accuracy not measured yet; cycles not measured yet; 0 extra kernels.

**An aten::grid_sampler instruction.** The chip has no instruction for aten::grid_sampler, so every aten::grid_sampler needs a workaround. It affects 36 operations in 2 models: 36 calls (0.22% of all calls) and MACs not counted (the capture does not size an ATen op); the biggest: aten::grid_sampler in PaddlePaddle/PP-DocLayoutV3_safetensors and aten::grid_sampler in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365. Cost today: 0 of 36 have a workaround (0 exact, 0 approximate), 0 failed and 36 wait for one; 85 workarounds proposed, 21 passing its check, 32 evaluated on a model; accuracy not measured yet; cycles not measured yet; 0 extra kernels.

**An integer format for indices.** No NX8 format can hold an integer index computed from the input, so the operations reading one (add, argmax, gather, repeat and topk) need a workaround. It affects 22 operations in 11 models: 22 calls (0.14% of all calls) and no MACs (data movement only); the biggest: repeat in PaddlePaddle/PP-DocLayoutV3_safetensors, repeat in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 and add in SamLowe/roberta-base-go_emotions. Cost today: 0 of 22 have a workaround (0 exact, 0 approximate), 0 failed and 22 wait for one; 58 workarounds proposed, 0 passing its check, 30 evaluated on a model; accuracy not measured yet; cycles not measured yet; 0 extra kernels.

**An upsample instruction.** The chip has no instruction for upsample, so every upsample needs a workaround. It affects 12 operations in 3 models: 12 calls (0.07% of all calls) and no MACs (data movement only); the biggest: upsample in PaddlePaddle/PP-DocLayoutV3_safetensors, upsample in mattmdjaga/segformer_b2_clothes and upsample in depth-anything/Depth-Anything-V2-Small-hf. Cost today: 0 of 12 have a workaround (0 exact, 0 approximate), 0 failed and 12 wait for one; 60 workarounds proposed, 39 passing its check, 26 evaluated on a model; accuracy not measured yet; cycles not measured yet; 0 extra kernels.

**An aten::concat instruction.** The chip has no instruction for aten::concat, so every aten::concat needs a workaround. It affects 3 operations in 2 models: 3 calls (0.02% of all calls) and MACs not counted (the capture does not size an ATen op); the biggest: aten::concat in PaddlePaddle/PP-DocLayoutV3_safetensors and aten::concat in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365. title: Missing instructions: 162 operations in 26 models need workarounds

body:
A kernel reads a tensor in the arrangement its writer stored it in; when the reader needs another arrangement, the reading kernel has to rearrange the data itself. This happens to 2335 of 4100 tensors passed between kernels (57%) in 38 models: 1873 for attention heads split or merged, 433 for other reshapes, 26 for pixels reordered and 3 for image patches.

The reading operations are 1,602 operations (1,602 calls, 9.93% of all calls; 338 G MACs, 6.42% of all MACs). The most common causes (writer → reader): linear → bmm (attention heads split or merged) 1575, linear → attention (attention heads split or merged) 207 and concat → bmm (other reshapes) 92; most in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (196), lcybuaa/Git-RSCLIP (146) and stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (128).

Cost today: extra cycles not measured yet (no reading kernel has run); 0 links fail.
title: Layout conversions: 2335 of 4100 tensors between kernels are rearranged

body:
Activations with no built-in function at the store (GELU, SiLU, tanh, …) go through a 256-entry lookup table (LUT), which limits their precision: 1,046 operations in 39 models (1,046 calls, 6.48% of all calls), most often gelu (372), silu (349) and gelu_tanh (102). Their quantized accuracy: worst -inf dB SQNR over 939 measured operations.

Kernels per forward pass (host launches, one per planned kernel call): median 25, most 232 (PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365, 232 planned groups), over 39 models.

FP32 headroom (how far the largest value is from FP32 overflow, in powers of ten) is least at 33.1 powers of ten for bmm in Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (largest value 2.75e+05).

183 outputs in 13 models hold a value at the FP32 limit itself (mostly add (166), select_where (14) and amin (2), e.g. an attention mask's fill value); they are counted apart from the headroom.

6 accuracy runs produced non-finite outputs (overflow or NaN).

0 kernels use over 80% of the 1,024-word instruction memory (IMEM) bank, of 7 kernels measured.
title: Resource limits: 1,046 operations limited by the LUT and up to 232 kernel launches per pass

body:
1. **The largest demonstrated cost is accuracy:** NX8 static 8-bit formats reduce prediction quality in 18 of 25 models with prediction metrics, including agreement falling from 100% to 0% in two models and Qwen perplexity rising from 16.5 to about 2,020; median output SQNR is 23.0 dB, while LUT-based activations reach −∞ dB and six accuracy runs produce non-finite outputs.
2. **Missing capabilities block direct execution:** eight gaps affect 139 operations across 18 models, with no operation-level workaround currently available; run-time addressing is the broadest gap, accounting for 65 operations in 17 models.
3. **Compute utilisation is very low in the limited measurements:** multiplier utilisation is 0% for unary and binary primitives, 16% for conv2d and at best 18% for row_norm, but primitive cycle shares and resulting end-to-end cycle penalties remain unmeasured.
4. **Layout handling adds widespread in-kernel work:** readers must rearrange 1,620 of 3,072 inter-kernel tensors (53%) across 28 models, predominantly for attention-head layouts, but no reading kernel has run to establish the extra cycles.
5. **Launch overhead is potentially substantial but not timed:** planned forward passes require a median 21 host kernel launches and up to 232; reported workaround-added kernels are zero because no operation has a deployed workaround, not evidence that fixing the gaps would be free.
